subject: Re: Capacity uplift & benchmark ask — MerchantForge renewal
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@merchantforge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@merchantforge.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: MerchantForge renewal — quick ask on throughput and term flexibility

Jordan —

We’re deep in the renewal review for MerchantForge and a couple of urgent items came up from engineering and procurement: 

- We need to validate end-to-end throughput for our live workload (avg 35 req/s, spikes to 120 req/s for 90s). Can you pull the latest perf numbers you referenced in the Q2 call?
- There’s a competing vendor offering an architecture with a per-request SLA and a 20% price improvement on comparable benchmarks — procurement wants us to run a short bakeoff unless we can present a credible contingency.
- Procurement is asking whether Redwood can offer a temporary capacity uplift and a term change (12-month fixed price for committed capacity) to avoid migration.

Attached is a short benchmarking brief (merchantforge_benchmark_request.pdf) with trace samples. Can we get a proposal by EOD Wednesday? We’re on a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, MerchantForge
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@merchantforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantForge renewal — quick ask on throughput and term flexibility

Tom —

Appreciate the context and the brief. Short answer: yes, we can support an accelerated benchmark and a temporary committed uplift while we work through a longer-term term amendment. Proposed immediate next steps: 

1) Quick perf baseline — Ben and Karthik will spin up a mirrored run using your traces and share a short report by Wednesday EOD. Expect: 95th p99 latency, token/sec, GPU utilization.
2) Contingent save proposal — I can put forward a 12-month fixed-price uplift (details below) plus a one-off credit to cover benchmark run costs.
3) Procurement alignment — if Priya can share the contract milestones we’ll draft a short amendment and flag any SOC/ops asks.

Prelim offer (subject to the baseline numbers):
- 25% committed capacity uplift (adds headroom to cover spikes)
- 12-month fixed-rate SKU at a 15% guidance discount vs current list (we can go to 20% if the baseline shows parity with the competitor on the three perf metrics)
- $10k credit to offset the bakeoff/engineering effort

Ben / Karthik — please see Tom’s brief attached and confirm the run plan.

Tom — I’ll follow up with a draft timeline and an MSA amendment for legal review.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@merchantforge.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantForge renewal — quick ask on throughput and term flexibility

All —

Plan for the baseline run: 
- Environment: prod-like GPU cluster (A100 x8), matching sequence lengths and batching patterns from the traces.
- Tests: steady-state at 35 req/s, 3x spike test up to 120 req/s for 90s, cold-start patterns, and a 10-min KV-cache warmup sweep.
- Deliverables: short deck + raw metrics CSV + annotated flamegraphs.

I’m attaching the run config we’ll use (benchmark_config.yaml) and I’ve looped in Ari Kaplan (vendor bench) to validate our harness for cross-vendor parity. If MerchantForge wants to run anything custom (auth flows, pre/post-processing), push samples to the Drive link and we’ll include them.

Attachments: benchmark_config.yaml (stub)

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@merchantforge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@merchantforge.com>, Ari Kaplan <ari@vendor-bench.com>
Date: 2027-07-13T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantForge renewal — quick ask on throughput and term flexibility

Jordan / Ben —

Thanks for the rapid response. A couple of updates from our side: 
- Procurement (Priya) has signaled that unless we get a 20% cost delta or a contract commitment that materially reduces migration risk, they’ll move forward with a bakeoff with the competitor next week.
- Security wants to ensure no data egress during the bench; we’ll need a short SOC-ops call if your baseline requires third-party instrumentation.

On the uplift offer: if Redwood can commit to a 12-month fixed price and guarantee the uplift for the pilot window (with the 20% floor if parity is shown), Procurement might remove the immediate bakeoff ask. That would buy us 6–8 weeks to finalize a thorough assessment.

Priya — can you confirm target contract milestones and if you’d accept a two-phase PO (pilot PO now, main PO on successful parity)?

Thanks,
Tom

On Mon, Jul 12, 2027 at 09:35 Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> All —
> 
> Plan for the baseline run: ... (see attachment)
> 
> Ben Carter
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@merchantforge.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@merchantforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-14T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantForge renewal — quick ask on throughput and term flexibility

Tom / Priya —

We can do the two-phase approach you outlined. Here’s a concrete save package we’ll put on paper today: 

1) Pilot phase (4 weeks):
   - 25% committed capacity uplift applied immediately for the pilot window
   - Pilot PO for 30% of uplift cost to cover benchmark infrastructure and support
   - $10k credit applied at invoice to offset bench effort
2) Contingent parity clause:
   - If baseline shows parity across p99 latency, throughput, and cost-per-1000-tokens with the competitor, Redwood will extend an additional 20% list discount for the 12-month fixed-price SKU and honor the uplift at the pilot rate for the full term.
3) Security & ops:
   - We’ll run the bench in a no-egress VPC and provide an ops contact for a short technical call (Ben + Karthik).

Next steps: 
- Ben: start the run on Monday and share results by EOD Wednesday.
- Priya: if you’re good with the two-phase PO, send the pilot PO amount and we’ll push an MSA amendment to legal. I’ll attach a draft MSA redline after this note.

If it helps, I can also schedule a brief exec sync with Marissa to lock the commercial terms today.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@merchantforge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@merchantforge.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@merchantforge.com>, Legal <legal@merchantforge.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-15T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantForge renewal — quick ask on throughput and term flexibility

Jordan —

We’ll proceed with the two-phase PO approach. Attached is the pilot PO and our MSA redline (MSA_redline.docx). Please note the following procurement items that must be addressed in the redline: 

- Clause on data handling during the bench (no external telemetry without prior written consent)
- Termination for convenience during pilot with 14-day notice
- Invoice schedule aligned with pilot PO milestone dates

I’ve flagged the parity clause and 20% discretionary approval to our finance lead; if you can include the contingency in the amendment, we’ll expedite.

Attachment: MSA_redline.docx (stub)

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Procurement, MerchantForge
